original_test_intent: Continuously exercise BMC SDR retrieval for 72 hours and verify sensor inventory/readings remain complete and plausible while the BMC stays functional.
original_method: Poll the full SDR list at an approved bounded interval, timestamp and validate every expected sensor against a firmware-matched identity/unit/status/range policy, retain raw anomalies, monitor BMC responsiveness and preserve diagnostics throughout the run.
manual_activity: Provide the firmware-matched SDR inventory, stable sensor identifiers, units, allowable states/ranges and valid-zero rules; approve the 72-hour polling interval, BMC-load ceiling, anomaly policy, watchdog and evidence-retention plan.
required_inputs: Per-sensor valid ranges and threshold semantics
Valid zero, unavailable and disabled rules
Pinned reviewed script/bundle revision or equivalent approved procedure
safety_requirements: Use a dedicated or approved recoverable BMC
Poll read-only at a bounded vendor-safe rate
Do not clear logs or sensor records
Stop on repeated timeout, load/latency growth, inventory drift or lost recovery
Do not treat every zero as invalid
Do not silently drop parse failures or unsupported units
agent_execution_scope: Capture complete baseline SDR and diagnostics
Run a bounded rehearsal across all sensor types
Validate count, identity, units, status and ranges per sample
Capture final sample and verify BMC functionality
engineer_actions: Provide SDR oracle and valid-zero semantics
Approve rate, duration and load thresholds

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `sdr elist` matches the source, but fixed cipher 17 is unvalidated and the proposal lacks an actual bounded loop. Checking a final tail cannot establish continuous completeness or sensor-specific correctness.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run secret-backed full `sdr elist` polling at the approved interval for 72 hours, timestamp and validate every complete sample against the sensor oracle, retain anomalies and continuously monitor BMC latency/resource health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The explicit 72-hour Procedure is preserved; the 720-minute Machine Time conflicts with it and is not substituted. Poll rate and acceptable missed samples are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a schema-aware sample pipeline that hashes full raw output, validates every expected sensor and separately tracks transport, parser, inventory and value anomalies over time.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces plaintext credentials, unbounded polling and end-only inspection with a controlled rate, sensor-specific oracle, per-sample evidence, BMC-load monitoring and safe retention.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates reported SDR availability and plausibility under polling load; it does not calibrate physical sensors, stimulate thresholds or prove accuracy against external instruments.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A zero can be valid for discrete or inactive sensors, while a temperature zero may or may not be plausible. Parser truncation can mimic missing sensors, and excessive evidence or request rate can itself destabilize the BMC.

project_override_considerations: Use project-defined stable sensor identity rather than display-name text alone, and preserve raw units/status. The 72-hour source requirement remains authoritative unless an approved decision resolves the conflicting 12-hour metadata.
expected_evidence: Approval, BMC/firmware and SDR oracle identity
Polling interval, total duration and tool/cipher versions
Per-sample complete raw hash and timestamp
Final BMC functionality and complete SDR sample
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure requires 72 hours, while Machine Time is 720 minutes (12 hours). The review preserves the explicit 72-hour Procedure and records the timing conflict without changing Master.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The SDR inventory, sensor policies, polling rate and load thresholds are identifiable package/approval inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Makes the endurance claim sample-complete and sensor-specific, prevents valid zeros or parser truncation from being misclassified, and preserves the 72-hour/12-hour source conflict.
independent_technical_reasoning: SDR output mixes analog readings, discrete states and unavailable/disabled entries, so one global 'zero is wrong' rule is technically invalid. A 72-hour test is about temporal continuity; a final sample cannot reveal missing intervals, transient timeouts or inventory drift. Stable identity, units and timestamped complete samples are required to distinguish real sensor anomalies from parser or transport failure. Polling itself consumes BMC resources, so request rate, latency and evidence growth must be bounded and observed.
